content.title: About
content.content: Watercress (Nasturtium officinale) is a leafy vegetable that grows in flowing water. It has bright green leaves, a mildly peppery taste, and a crunchy texture. Watercress is usually eaten raw in salads, smoothies, and as a garnish.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Watercress is considered one of the most nutrient‑dense leafy greens.
It naturally occurs in streams and rivers across Europe, Asia, and North America.
Ancient Romans used it as a medicinal herb for colds.
It is exceptionally high in vitamin C – about 70 mg per 100 g, more than oranges.
The leaves can be used as a natural food coloring.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C boosts immunity and protects cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Contains vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Source of folate
items.content: Folate supports cell division and is especially important during pregnancy.

items.title: High in antioxidants
items.content: Watercress provides carotenoids and polyphenols that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Low‑calorie fiber source
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Water‑borne contamination
items.content: Because it grows in streams, watercress can be contaminated with bacteria or parasites; thorough washing is recommended.

items.title: Interaction with blood thinners
items.content: High vitamin K content may reduce the effectiveness of anticoagulant medications.

items.title: Allergic reactions
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergy symptoms such as rash or swelling.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Add watercress to fresh salads, sandwiches, smoothies, soups, or use it as a garnish for fish and meat dishes. Before eating, rinse the leaves well under running water.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store watercress in the refrigerator in an airtight container or a bag with a small amount of moisture. It stays fresh for 3–5 days. Discard if leaves turn yellow or develop an off‑odor.
